disease_label_per_paper: Early malignant syphilis as a rare form of secondary syphilis
presentation_summary: 29-year-old woman presented with a 6-week history of fever to 38.5 C, loss of appetite, and myalgia followed by extensive erythematous nodular rash.
The rash involved scalp, face, neck, axilla, trunk, back, palms, soles, and perineal area; some perineal lesions were ulcerated and painless.
At examination she was afebrile with stable vital signs and good general condition.
Oral and genital mucosa were spared; there were no ophthalmologic or neurologic abnormalities.
CBC was normal. RPR was reactive at 1:128 and a Treponema pallidum test was positive; HIV, HCV, and HBV serology were negative.
Skin biopsy showed subcorneal pustules and non-caseating granulomas with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate.
She received benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units once weekly for 3 weeks, had no Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, and skin lesions rapidly healed during the following month.

outcome.summary: No Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction occurred. Lesions rapidly healed during the month after penicillin administration; RPR titer fell to 1:4 after 3 months.

quality_warnings: RPR, treponemal serology, viral serologies, and biopsy pathology are confirmatory/context evidence and are marked use_in_ranking:false.
This case is a severe ulceronodular phenotype of secondary syphilis, but the expected manifold remains D-SECONDARY-SYPHILIS rather than a separate malignant-syphilis disease id.
